```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

sheepdog writes two tables that occupancy models with false positives, such
as those of the crywolf package, read: `clip_manifest.csv`
(`extract_validation_clips()`) and `validation_by_clip.csv`
(`post_validation()`). This document fixes their columns, types and the
definition of an occasion. The two packages are independent: sheepdog does
not depend on crywolf, and crywolf reads these files without loading
sheepdog.

Example files ship with the package:

```{r}
library(sheepdog)
manifest   <- system.file("extdata", "clip_manifest.csv", package = "sheepdog")
validation <- system.file("extdata", "validation_by_clip.csv",
                          package = "sheepdog")
v <- readr::read_csv(validation, show_col_types = FALSE)
v[, c("site", "occasion_id", "confidence", "n_detections_occasion",
      "inclusion_prob", "verdict")]
```

They come from a `"random_detections"` run (occasion = file, threshold 0.5)
on simulated data (`data-raw/make_extdata.R`).

## Occasion

An occasion is the sampling unit of the occupancy model, set by
`occasion_unit`:

- `"file"`: one recording. `occasion_id` is the file name without
  extension, e.g. `ARA01_20220110_193000`.
- `"minute"`: one minute of a recording, from `file_offset`.
  `occasion_id` is `<file>_m<minute>`, with the minute zero-based and padded
  to three digits, e.g. `ARA01_20220110_193000_m002` for 120-180 s.

The site, species and occasion (`site`, `species_code`, `occasion_id`)
identify the detection history cell. With minute occasions, match them to
the occasions of the model by file and minute of `clip_start`.

## clip_manifest.csv

One row per clip. Columns, in this order:

| column | type | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `site` | character | Site: the folder of the selection table, without the `output_` prefix. |
| `species_code` | character | Classifier label, e.g. `Boana raniceps_boa-ran`. |
| `species_folder` | character | Short species code used as folder name, e.g. `boa_ran`. |
| `recording_date` | character `YYYYMMDD` | Date in the recording file name. |
| `night` | character `YYYYMMDD` | Grouping date: equals `recording_date`, or the day before for small hours when the hour window crosses midnight. |
| `recording_hour` | character `HH` | Hour in the recording file name. |
| `rank` | integer | `"top"`: rank by confidence in the site x species x night x hour stratum. `"random_detections"`: order of the clip in its occasion (by `file_offset`). `NA` in `"random_recordings"`. |
| `confidence` | double | BirdNET confidence score. `NA` for whole-recording clips (`"random_recordings"`). |
| `clip_file` | character | File name of the clip (`<conf>_<rank>_<recording>_<start>s_<end>s.wav`, or `rec_<site>_<species>_<occasion_id>.wav` for whole recordings). |
| `clip_start`, `clip_end` | double (s) | Start and end of the clip in the source recording. `clip_end` is `NA` for whole recordings of unknown length. |
| `duration` | double (s) | `clip_end - clip_start`. |
| `source_audio` | character | Path of the source recording, after remapping. |
| `begin_path` | character | Path as written in the selection table (`Begin Path`). |
| `status` | character | `ok`, `already_exists`, `audio_not_found`, `simulated` or `error: <message>`. |
| `sampling_mode` | character | `top`, `random_detections` or `random_recordings`. |
| `occasion_id` | character | Occasion (see above). |
| `n_detections_occasion` | integer | Predictions of the species with confidence >= `threshold` in the occasion. `NA` when no `threshold` was given. |
| `inclusion_prob` | double | Probability that the occasion (or recording) was drawn. `NA` in `"top"`, which is not a probability sample. |

In `"random_detections"`, every prediction >= `threshold` of a drawn
occasion is cut, so the number of clips of the occasion equals
`n_detections_occasion`. This is the assumption of the
observation-confirmation design (Chambert et al. 2015,
<https://doi.org/10.1890/14-1507.1>): every detection of a checked occasion
is checked.

## validation_by_clip.csv

The manifest plus two columns:

| column | type | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `verdict` | character | `positive` (true detection), `negative` (false positive), `not_reviewed` (clip found in the review folder, but in no subfolder matching the positive or negative pattern, e.g. still in the species folder) or `clip_missing` (clip not found in the review folder). |
| `reviewed_path` | character | Path where the reviewed clip was found; `NA` when missing. |

Only `positive` and `negative` are reviewed verdicts. Clips of
`"random_recordings"` (`confidence = NA`) are the second method of a
multiple-method design (Miller et al. 2011,
<https://doi.org/10.1890/10-1396.1>), that is, manual annotation of
recordings. They are not confirmations of detections and must not go to the
`validation` argument of `crywolf::fp_aggregate()`.

## Export for occupancy models

`export_occupancy_data()` writes in one folder everything an occupancy
model with false positives needs: every occasion, the classifier scores,
the reviewed clips with their design and, optionally, covariates of the
occasions and posterior draws of a Bayesian calibration. The folder follows
the schema `sheepdog-occupancy`, version 1.1, described below. The tables are plain CSV files (missing values
are empty cells); the calibration draws are a Parquet file.

```{r, message = FALSE}
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")
det <- read_selection_tables(file.path(ex, "birdnet"))
out <- export_occupancy_data(
  file.path(tempdir(), "occupancy"), det,
  recordings = file.path(ex, "recordings.csv"),
  validation = list.files(file.path(ex, "validation"), full.names = TRUE)
)
vapply(out$tables, nrow, integer(1))
```

The example clips were drawn with `"top"`, so `validation.csv` serves the
calibration but not the false-positive rate of an occupancy model (see
`sampling_mode` below).

### schema.json

| field | definition |
|---|---|
| `schema`, `schema_version` | `"sheepdog-occupancy"` and `1.1`. Minor versions only add tables, columns or fields, so a reader of version 1 can read any 1.x by ignoring what it does not know; it should refuse other names and major versions. Version 1.1 added the occasion covariates and the calibration keys; version 1.2, `occasion_draws.parquet`. |
| `created`, `sheepdog_version`, `classifier` | Provenance of the export. |
| `occasion_unit` | `"file"` or `"minute"` (see Occasion above). |
| `min_confidence` | Scores below this value were not written: an occasion x species pair absent from `scores.csv` had no prediction at or above it. |
| `dawn_hour` | Recordings before this hour belong to the night before. |
| `sites`, `species` | Every site and every classifier label (`species_code`) of the export. |
| `tables` | For each table, its file and number of rows. |
| `occasion_covariates` | The columns of `occasions.csv` after the fixed ones (from `occasion_covariates` and the calibration keys), when any. |
| `occasion_draws` | Written by `occasion_draws()` (version 1.2): `file`, `rule`, `p_min` (with `"threshold"`), `seed` (with `"sample"`), `n_draws` and `species`. |
| `calibration` | With `fit`: `engine`, `formula`, `n_draws`, `grid_step`, `grid_min`, `keys` (the columns that identify a row of `calibration_draws.parquet` within a draw: `site`, `species`, the `calibration_keys` and `grid_index`) and `new_levels` (`"uncertainty"`: levels of a key absent from the calibration data are drawn from the distribution of the group). |

### occasions.csv

One row per occasion, with or without predictions, from the list of
recordings (`recordings`).

| column | type | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `site`, `occasion_id` | character | The occasion (see Occasion above). |
| `source_audio` | character | Path of the recording. |
| `recording_date`, `recording_hour` | character | Date (`YYYYMMDD`) and hour (`HH`) in the file name. |
| `night` | character `YYYYMMDD` | Night of the occasion: the day before for recordings before `dawn_hour`. |
| `start`, `duration` | double (s) | Start of the occasion in the recording (0 for files) and its length (`NA` when unknown). |
| further columns | any | Covariates of the occasion from `occasion_covariates`, and the calibration keys, always written as text (e.g. `month`, `YYYYMM`, derived from `recording_date` when not given). |

### detections.csv and scores.csv

`detections.csv` has one row per prediction with confidence >=
`min_confidence`: `site`, `occasion_id`, `species_code`, `species` (the
short code of `species_folder`, the key of the calibration), `file_offset`
(s) and `confidence`. `scores.csv` summarises them by occasion x species:
`max_score` (the highest confidence) and `n_above_min` (the number of
predictions). Pairs absent from `scores.csv` are censored at
`min_confidence`.

### validation.csv and recordings_verified.csv

`validation.csv` holds the clips of the `"top"` and `"random_detections"`
designs: `site`, `occasion_id`, `species_code`, `species`, `clip_start`,
`clip_end`, `confidence`, `sampling_mode`, `inclusion_prob`,
`n_detections_occasion`, `verdict` (as in `validation_by_clip.csv`, or
`disagreement` after `consensus_verdicts()`) and `tp` (1 for `positive`,
0 for `negative`, empty otherwise), plus `reviewer` and `n_reviewers` when
present. Only clips of `"random_detections"` estimate a false-positive
rate; `"top"` clips serve the calibration.

`recordings_verified.csv` holds the occasions annotated by ear
(`"random_recordings"`), with `present` (1, 0 or empty) in place of `tp`.
The two tables are kept apart because they say different things: a
positive clip proves that the species called in its occasion, a negative
clip only that this prediction was false (the species may have called
with a lower score), while an annotated recording gives the state of the
whole occasion.

### sites.csv

One row per site, with the covariates given in `sites`.

### calibration_draws.parquet

With `fit` (a model of `fit_calibration(engine = "brms")`), `n_draws`
draws of the posterior of P(TP) on a grid of scores from `min_confidence`
in steps of `grid_step`, for each site x species with predictions:
`draw`, `site`, `species`, one text column per calibration key,
`grid_index`, `confidence` (the grid point) and `p_tp`. A detection takes
the value of the grid point nearest its score, as in `score_detections()`,
and of the levels of the keys of its occasion in `occasions.csv`. Every
level of a key found among the occasions of a site is covered. Species
absent from the calibration are left out; sites and key levels absent from
it are drawn as new levels of their group. Reading it needs
the 'arrow' package (in R) or any Parquet reader.

### occasion_draws.parquet

Written into an export by `occasion_draws()`: for each calibration draw,
the detection `y` of every occasion with at least one prediction of the
species (`draw`, `site`, `occasion_id`, `species` as the short code, `y`
as a 32-bit integer). `y` is 1 when at least one prediction of the
occasion is judged true in that draw, 0 when none is, and empty when the
occasion cannot be scored (a prediction without calibration draws). The
other occasions of `occasions.csv` are 0 in every draw. With
`rule = "sample"` a prediction is judged true at random with its
probability of being true; with `"threshold"`, when that probability is at
least `p_min`. Fitting the occupancy model to each draw and pooling the
posteriors propagates the uncertainty of the calibration (Monte Carlo
propagation); `crywolf::fp_draws_data()` reads the table when its settings
match the request and otherwise draws the same detections itself.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
occasion_draws(file.path(tempdir(), "occupancy"), rule = "sample",
               n_draws = 50, seed = 2026)
```

## End to end: the Curiango data

This section runs the whole flow, from the classifier scores to the
occupancy estimates, on real data: the Common Pauraque (*Nyctidromus
albicollis*) recordings of Piatti et al. (data:
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21795898>; article:
<https://doi.org/10.1002/jav.03737>). The models take hours, so the code
below is not run here; the results are read from tables cached in the
package, written by `dev/benchmarks/curiango-export.R` and
`dev/benchmarks/curiango-flow.R` of the source repository.

The recorders took one-minute recordings at four sites; the occasion is
the recording (`occasion_unit = "file"`), grouped into nights at each
recorder, the sites of the occupancy model. Two classifiers scored them:
a custom one and BirdNET. About 1% of the recordings, drawn in proportion
to the effort of each site without looking at the scores, were annotated
by ear; each annotated minute with a score is a reviewed clip of the
observation-confirmation design, and the calibration is fitted to these
clips.

```{r, include = FALSE}
flow <- function(file) {
  read.csv(system.file("benchmarks", paste0("curiango-flow-", file, ".csv"),
                       package = "sheepdog"))
}
```

### 1. Export

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fit <- fit_calibration(val_cal, tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | site), engine = "brms",
                       prior = calibration_prior(tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | site),
                                                 val_cal),
                       chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 2026)
export_occupancy_data(
  "curiango/custom", detections, recordings = recordings,
  validation = validation, fit = fit,
  occasion_covariates = covariates, # night_site_id, temp, rh, moon, bio, aci
  min_confidence = 0.1, n_draws = 100, seed = 2026)
```

The model of the calibration is chosen by cross-validated log-loss among
`tp ~ logit_conf` and `tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | site)` (custom classifier:
with the site; BirdNET: without), and fitted with 'brms' with the prior of
`calibration_prior()` (see `vignette("bayesian-calibration")`).

### 2. Check the calibration

Before the calibration draws are used, the calibration must reproduce the
data it was fitted to: the share of true positives overall, by score bin,
by site and by month.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ppc <- calibration_ppc(fit, val_cal, group = "month")
plot_calibration_ppc(ppc, check = "month")
```

```{r}
ppc <- flow("ppc")
ppc_n <- aggregate(cbind(groups = 1, flagged = flagged) ~ classifier + check,
                   data = ppc, FUN = sum)
ppc_n[order(ppc_n$classifier, ppc_n$check), ]
month <- ppc[ppc$check == "month" & ppc$flagged,
             c("classifier", "group", "n", "observed", "pred_mean", "p_value")]
month[4:6] <- lapply(month[4:6], round, 3)
month
```

Both calibrations reproduce the overall share of true positives, but not
the share by month: in some months nearly every reviewed minute was a true
detection, in others almost none, beyond what the score predicts. The
probability that a prediction is true depends on how much the species
called that month, which a calibration on the score alone (and the site)
does not see. The draws below inherit this misfit. A calibration with the
month (`tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | month)`, exported with
`calibration_keys = "month"`) removes it, but the month then carries
calling activity into P(TP), and the reviewed minutes inform both the
calibration and the occupancy model; it is a sensitivity analysis here,
not the recommended model.

### 3. Versions of the detections

```{r, eval = FALSE}
occasion_draws("curiango/custom", rule = "sample", n_draws = 20, seed = 2026)
```

Each version is one draw of which predictions are true; an occasion is a
detection when at least one of its predictions is. The share of minutes
with a detection per version:

```{r}
versions <- flow("versions")
aggregate(detection_rate ~ classifier, data = versions,
          FUN = function(x) round(c(mean = mean(x), min = min(x), max = max(x)), 4))
```

### 4. Occupancy in crywolf

crywolf reads the export, takes the versions from `occasion_draws.parquet`
(its `fp_draws_data()` draws the same ones when the table is absent),
fits the occupancy model with false positives to each version and pools
the posteriors in equal shares.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
x <- crywolf::fp_read_sheepdog("curiango/custom", species = "nyc_alb")
versions <- crywolf::fp_draws_data(x, rule = "sample", n_draws = 20,
                                   seed = 2026, occasions = occ, sites = nights,
                                   site = "night_site_id")
mc <- crywolf::fp_occu_mc(versions, occ = ~ temp + rh + moon,
                          det = ~ bio + aci, fp = ~ 1, seed = 1,
                          parallel = TRUE)
summary(mc)
```

`occ` holds the minute covariates (`bio`, `aci`) and `nights` the night
covariates (`temp`, `rh`, `moon`), all standardised.

```{r}
fits <- flow("fits")
aggregate(cbind(fits = 1, kept = kept, divergences = divergences) ~ classifier,
          data = fits, FUN = sum)
s <- flow("summary")
s <- s[grepl("^occ_|^p10_ref$|^p11_ref$", s$variable),
       c("classifier", "variable", "mean", "sd", "sd_within", "sd_between",
         "share_between")]
s[-1:-2] <- lapply(s[-1:-2], round, 3)
s
```

`sd_within` is the posterior uncertainty given one version of the
detections, and `sd_between` the uncertainty about which detections are
true; their squares add up to the pooled variance (`share_between` is the
share of the second). Every fit converged (largest R-hat
`r round(max(fits$max_rhat), 3)`, no divergent transitions).

With the custom classifier, most of the posterior variance of the
occupancy intercept and of the humidity effect comes from the calibration:
which of its many low-scoring predictions are true changes from version to
version, and a model fitted to any one version alone would report about
half the posterior standard deviation. BirdNET
gives few predictions, most of them confident, so its versions differ
little and the uncertainty is mostly within each fit. The two classifiers
also disagree on the temperature effect; with the misfit of the
calibrations by month, this comparison is a demonstration of the flow, not
an ecological result.

## Files written by v1.2.0

Up to v1.2.0 the same tables were written in Portuguese
(`manifesto_clipes.csv`, `validacao_por_clipe.csv`). sheepdog reads them and
renames on reading. The map is:

| v1.2.0 | v2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `local` | `site` |
| `pasta_especie` | `species_folder` |
| `data_gravacao` | `recording_date` |
| `noite` | `night` |
| `hora_gravacao` | `recording_hour` |
| `arquivo_clipe` | `clip_file` |
| `inicio_clipe`, `fim_clipe`, `duracao` | `clip_start`, `clip_end`, `duration` |
| `audio_origem` | `source_audio` |
| `begin_path_original` | `begin_path` |
| `modo_amostragem` | `sampling_mode` |
| `ocasiao_id` | `occasion_id` |
| `n_deteccoes_ocasiao` | `n_detections_occasion` |
| `prob_inclusao` | `inclusion_prob` |
| `veredito` | `verdict` |
| `caminho_wav` | `reviewed_path` |

Values: `aleatorio_deteccoes` and `aleatorio_gravacoes` become
`random_detections` and `random_recordings`; `positivo`, `negativo`,
`nao_validado` and `clipe_ausente` become `positive`, `negative`,
`not_reviewed` and `clip_missing`; `ja_existia`, `audio_nao_encontrado`,
`simulado` and `erro:` become `already_exists`, `audio_not_found`,
`simulated` and `error:`. Whole-recording clips cut by v1.2.0 keep their
`grav_` prefix on disk; new ones use `rec_`.

## Reading the validation in crywolf

```{r, eval = FALSE}
v <- crywolf::fp_read_validation(validation)
```

`fp_read_validation()` reads the v1.2.0 format; reading the column names
above needs a crywolf version that supports them.
